As of 415 PM Wednesday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... Strong and gusty nely winds will accompany 
widespread rain that will soak cntl NC with mostly from 2-5" through 
Thu morning, with locally higher amounts possible through the 
Coastal Plain and adjacent ern Piedmont and Sandhills.  

GOES-E water vapor satellite data and model forecasts depict a 
strongly dynamic mid/upr-level pattern evolving across the Southeast 
today. Within that pattern, a couple of closely-spaced subtropical 
perturbations are evident in water vapor satellite data just 
offshore the FL Atlantic and Gulf coasts, respectively, and are 
forecast to assume negative tilt while pivoting up the South 
Atlantic coast through early Thu. They may be "captured by" and 
phase with a synoptic trough comprised of a vigorous nrn stream 
shortwave trough along the cntl Gulf Coast and a cyclone digging 
across the cntl Plains and mid MS Valley, which themselves are 
forecast to become increasingly-phased and amplified while also 
assuming negative tilt across the Southeast through early Thu. 
Standardized 500 mb height anomalies are forecast to exceed -5 sigma 
within the basal portion of that synoptic trough as it pivots across 
nrn FL tonight, indicative of how anomalous this dynamic pattern 
will become. An intense cyclone will then lift newd and across the 
TN/OH Valleys through Thu night and the nrn Middle Atlantic on Fri. 

At the surface, a ~1041 mb cP high now centered over coastal ME, and 
which appeared to peak in strength at 1044 mb along the NY/ON border 
late this morning, will continue to weaken and progress offshore 
through Thu. Meanwhile, at least three areas of low pressure have 
become evident in satellite and surface observational data over the 
nern Gulf and flanking South FL, respectively. The models indicate 
the ern-most of those lows will become dominant and deepen quite 
rapidly, from around 1008 mb this afternoon to around 995 mb over 
sern NC by Thu morning, then occlude while tracking generally nwd 
and across the NC Coastal Plain or ern Piedmont through early Thu 
afternoon. A secondary, triple point wave may develop and track 
nearer the Middle Atlantic and srn New England coast through Thu 
night. The track of the occluding low, after having continued a wwd 
trend in 00Z guidance, has shifted slightly ewd in 12Z guidance and 
very near the consensus track from 24 hours ago. Such a track has 
further increased confidence in the heaviest rainfall amounts just 
to its east and across the Coastal Plain and adjacent ern Piedmont 
and Sandhills; and within that corridor, there has been an increased 
signal in hi-resolution guidance for 5-8" and locally near 10", 
within the broader and "lesser" 2-5" amounts depicted in both 
dynamical and AI-based global guidance. If such amounts in excess of 
5" should occur, the risk of scattered instances of flash flooding 
would be much greater, relative to what would otherwise be a minor, 
poor drainage and urban flood risk.  

Aside from the widespread and significant rainfall, strong nely 
winds will also result and probably increase through the evening-
night. While the official forecast calls for wind gusts up to 35-40 
kts overnight, the potential exists for even stronger gusts, when 
intense wind fields develop and expand along and immediately 
surrounding an intense pressure fall/rise couplet accompanying the 
aforementioned, deepening cyclone. However, there remains 
uncertainty regarding to what degree those intense winds just above 
the shallow boundary layer (ie. within the overcast/cloud layer 
above) will mix to the surface, particularly given nocturnal timing 
when near surface lapse rates will otherwise be at a diurnal minimum 
and oppose consistent momentum transfer. The strongest gusts may 
consequently be more sporadic and coincide with areas of heavier 
rain, where drag-induced transfer of momentum into the boundary 
layer would be most likely. Winds will then lessen through 
Thu and early evening, as the primary low lifts north and occludes. 

While weak elevated instability tonight will support a slight chance 
of thunder throughout cntl NC, thunder potential will be relatively 
maximized over and especially just east of the nrn and cntl Coastal 
Plain Thu morning, where a narrow moist/warm sector may become 
briefly and marginally supportive of surface-based convection. 
Strongly veering and intense wind profiles in that area would 
conditionally support a risk of mini-superells and isolated 
tornadoes, which at this time appears to be favored just to the east 
of RAH's counties. 


KEY MESSAGE 2... A secondary surge of strong winds/gusts, this time 
from the southwest, will likely develop across the Carolinas Thu 
night through early Fri.
